A clearer journey.

A working concept for CamTran’s next website, demonstrating how simpler rider tools and clearer staff workflows can support the goals of RFP 26-05.

Independent proposal sample. Not an official CamTran site. Arrivals, itineraries, stop sequences, timetables, alerts, and events are illustrative. No live transit feed, payment processing, authentication, or production CMS is connected.

Explore the rider experience ↗

Five things to try.

01 / FIND A CONNECTION

From destination to route.

Search “Galleria” or “18”, filter urban/rural service, and open a route. Switch directions, choose weekday or Saturday sample times, inspect the schematic and route-specific notices, and download a clearly labeled sample timetable.

Try route discovery →

02 / UNDERSTAND THE NEXT ARRIVAL

Useful information at a glance.

Choose among three route previews. The board updates while clearly identifying the arrivals as demonstration data.

Try arrival previews →

03 / PLAN WITH CONFIDENCE

A focused planning experience.

Choose two sample destinations, swap them, and explore a sample route. Equal origin and destination values trigger a helpful validation message. This is a bounded scenario demonstration, not a routing engine.

Try the trip panel →

04 / REMOVE LANGUAGE FRICTION

English and Spanish.

Use ES / EN to switch the core homepage copy and primary navigation. The rider interface includes bilingual content, labels and notices. Production still requires linguistic review, automated translation and translation management.

Try the language switch →

05 / GIVE STAFF A SIMPLER WORKFLOW

Try the CMS editor.

The website reads every alert, route, fare, news item and event through one CMS adapter. The editor demo drives that adapter with role-based permissions (editor, approver, administrator), a draft → review → approve → publish workflow, scheduling windows, English/Spanish fields, version history with restore, and an audit log. Open the public site in a second tab, publish an alert as an approver, and watch it appear without a reload.

Demo script: 1) As Editor, create an emergency alert and submit it for review (note that Publish is not offered). 2) Switch to Approver, approve and publish. 3) Watch the public banner change, then toggle Spanish. 4) Restore an earlier version as a draft and confirm the existing published alert remains visible until the replacement is approved and published. Compare versions in the history panel.

Boundary: this runs on sample data stored in this browser. Production connects the adapter to the DYD CMS over its API, with real accounts, MFA, shared persistence and server-side permission enforcement.

Proposed delivery approach.

Illustrative 24-week plan, subject to discovery, content readiness, integration access, and agreement. The RFP target is no more than nine months unless otherwise proposed.

  1. Weeks 1–3 · Discover. Stakeholder workshops, rider tasks, analytics/content review, accessibility and technical assessment.
  2. Weeks 4–7 · Design. Sitemap, wireframes, responsive design system and rider validation.
  3. Weeks 8–15 · Build. CMS configuration, route integrations, alerts, translation and content migration.
  4. Weeks 16–20 · Verify. Accessibility, security, browsers, performance, migration and user acceptance testing.
  5. Weeks 21–24 · Launch. Staff training, recovery rehearsal, final remediation and monitored cutover.
  6. After launch · Support. At least twelve months of support, with priced service levels and agreed response/resolution commitments.

Bid preparation notes.

The prototype supplements the required bid package.

The RFP describes sealed submission and mandatory forms. Its evaluation considers responsiveness, experience, references, quality and cost; Attachment U requests at least three similar references within five years. A prototype does not substitute for those materials. Confirm current addenda and whether a hosted link or USB/offline sample is permitted.

Questions to resolve through the procurement channel.
  • Which CMS, hosting, transit feeds and API agreements currently exist?
  • Are GTFS, realtime arrivals and service alert feeds available for both urban and rural service?
  • What content volume, document remediation and translation review are expected?
  • What recovery targets and critical support response/resolution times are expected?
  • The pre-bid section contains both 1:30 PM and 10 AM; request written clarification.
  • Confirm applicability of construction-related clauses and required bond/insurance instruments to this website scope.
